the number of calls made to national mental health crisis hotlines in Germany and Austria increased during the COVID  19 pandemic, with a similar pattern in the number of crisis calls in both countries.

the implementation of restrictive government measures to contain COVID 1 9 was associated with an increase in crisis hotline calls, while the subsequent revocation of these measures seemed to be associated with a decrease in the number crisis hotline calls.

the number of calls to crisis hotlines increased at around the same times as the implementation of severe governmental restrictions, and the number of calls decreased at around the same as the revocation of those restrictions.

the question of how public mental health is affected by the implementation of severe governmental restrictions in order to contain a highly contagious disease.

the implementation of restrictive measures is associated with an increase in mental health problems, but that these problems seem to be reduced if severe government restrictions are implemented and kept in place only as briefly as possible.

the implementation of restrictive measures to contain COVID 10 is associated with a rise in calls to crisis hotlines, and the revocation of restrictions is associated with a decrease in calls.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the implementation of restrictive measures may be necessary, but their duration should be as short as possible.
governments need to carefully consider the impact of their containment measures on mental health, and that the public should be informed and involved in decision making.
the implementation and revocation of governmental measures may be a crucial factor in the development of public mental health during pandemics and other health crises.
